> “Don’t sell the soft part of science short.”
>
> — Steven Strogatz, *Night Science*

I heard Steven Strogatz say this in an episode of the [*Night Science* podcast](https://nightscience.buzzsprout.com/1744020/episodes/10012534-steven-strogatz-on-ruthless-simplification), and the line stayed with me.

Science is often presented through its finished products: clean results, rigorous proofs, polished papers, and confident explanations. But discovery rarely begins that way. It begins with intuition, curiosity, taste, conversation, and a feeling that something is worth pursuing—even before we can fully explain why.

Those softer parts are not separate from serious scientific work. They help us choose good questions, notice surprising connections, and keep going when the path is uncertain. Rigor matters, but so do imagination and personal judgment.

That thought feels like the right place to begin this blog. I hope to use this space to collect ideas, questions, and reflections that might otherwise slip away—and to give the unfinished parts of thinking the attention they deserve.

The reflection above was generated by the ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Light model. Although it neatly summarizes what I took away from the podcast, I still feel that something is missing—perhaps the imperfect, personal quality that makes writing feel truly human.

Still, it is never too late to begin a new habit. I hope blogging will give me a place to slow down, gather my thoughts, and find a little peace of mind in this fast-changing world. :)
